problem: Scaling instruction tuning of large language models to heterogeneous mixtures is hindered by gradient interference between different tasks and bandwidth-heavy synchronization across devices.
approach: MERIT partitions the instruction-tuning mixture along top PCA conflict axes to identify and separate gradient conflicts, then fine-tunes each partition independently without inter-partition communication before merging the results via token-weighted averaging.
contribution: On Qwen2.5-VL-3B with 136 Vision-FLAN tasks, MERIT improves the 8-benchmark average from 54.3 (joint training) to 57.0, and scales to a 7B model on 1.6M-example, 176-source mixture while matching centralized joint training with minimal overhead.

problem: Hybrid sequence models combining Transformers and state-space models lack a basic understanding of when and why they outperform their constituent models.
approach: The paper proves theoretical bounds on parameter requirements and working memory for non-hybrid models on synthetic tasks, then constructs explicit hybrid models (selective copying, associative recall) that avoid these limitations by leveraging both mechanisms.
contribution: On core synthetic tasks, hybrid models achieve optimal performance with small size and working memory, and empirically learned hybrids outperform non-hybrids with up to 6x as many parameters, with stronger length generalization and robustness.

problem: The Gaussian mechanism is widely used for differential privacy, but its optimality as dimension grows is unproven; low-dimensional privacy-utility tradeoffs may be improved.
approach: The paper proves asymptotic optimality of the Gaussian mechanism in high dimensions and introduces Spherical Generalized Gamma DP mechanisms, a family that contains the Gaussian and ℓ2 mechanisms, identifying members with better low-dimensional performance.
contribution: Establishes that no additive-noise mechanism can asymptotically improve on the Gaussian mechanism's privacy-utility tradeoff in high dimensions, and provides tight composition results for the new mechanism family.

problem: Multi-domain graph pre-training jointly trains all source domains, incurring high computational cost and redundancy, with unclear evidence that all domain data contributes equally to effective transfer.
approach: MDGMIX selects boundary nodes to construct challenging mixed-domain subgraphs and decouples shared patterns from domain-specific patterns via coarse-grained and fine-grained discrimination losses, with lightweight prompt weighting during adaptation.
contribution: MDGMIX consistently outperforms baselines in few-shot classification while exhibiting superior time and memory efficiency, reducing redundancy in multi-domain graph pre-training.

problem: Test-time noise optimization for reward-guided generation suffers from reward hacking and is too slow for practical use; there is a need to prevent hacking while enabling efficient ascent.
approach: Gradient preconditioning projects reward gradients onto a white Gaussian noise feasible set with blockwise norm constraints, reshaping updates into noise-aligned directions that prevent reward hacking while enabling faster convergence.
contribution: On FLUX with four reward models, the approach reaches comparable Aesthetic Score using only 30% of the wall-clock time required by state-of-the-art regularization methods, with negligible FFT-matching overhead.

problem: Theoretical bounds on the Lipschitz constant of neural networks show only logarithmic growth in width for ReLU networks at initialization, but empirically the constant does not increase with width, leaving a theory-practice gap.
approach: The paper establishes finite-width, non-asymptotic upper bounds on the local Lipschitz constant for smooth-activation networks both at random initialization and throughout lazy training.
contribution: Proves that the local Lipschitz constant of deep neural networks does not increase with network width, closing the gap between empirical observations and prior theoretical findings.

problem: Multimodal LLMs exhibit vision-language misalignment where textual responses are not factually aligned with image-text inputs, partly because causal attention limits earlier modalities (images) from attending to later ones (text).
approach: Replace causal attention with modality-mutual attention (MMA) that enables image tokens to attend to text tokens, allowing cross-modal information flow to correct vision-language misalignment without adding parameters.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across 12 multimodal understanding benchmarks with +6.2% average improvement across 3 LLM backbones without introducing additional parameters.

problem: Tabular foundation models based on Transformers have quadratic complexity in dataset size, increasing training and inference overhead and limiting capacity for large-scale tabular data.
approach: TACO compresses the training dataset in a latent space via end-to-end compression, enabling in-context learning without requiring the full dataset as context.
contribution: On TabArena benchmark, TACO is up to 94x faster in inference, consumes up to 97% less memory compared to state-of-the-art tabular Transformers, while retaining performance and scaling better with increased dataset sizes.

problem: Diffusion-based reinforcement learning policies have high training and inference overhead due to their iterative generative processes, limiting practical applicability.
approach: MFPO replaces diffusion policies with MeanFlow models, few-step flow-based policies optimized via soft policy iteration under maximum entropy RL framework, addressing likelihood evaluation and soft policy improvement challenges specific to flow policies.
contribution: Achieves performance comparable to or exceeding diffusion-based RL baselines on MuJoCo, DeepMind Control Suite, and HumanoidBench while considerably reducing training and inference time.

problem: Code documentation is designed for human readers, but autonomous coding agents need documentation as executable repo-specific playbooks; conventional refinement methods suffer from output coupling where fixing one entity breaks its dependents.
approach: DocSearch formulates agent-oriented documentation generation as black-box optimization over documentation space; it uses a dependency-guided bi-level search where the outer level prioritizes refinement via the program-entity DAG and the inner level performs beam search over documentation refinements.
contribution: On DevEval+ with GPT-4o, DocSearch achieves 90.7% solve rate, outperforming the strongest baseline by 32.6%, with documented knowledge transferring effectively across programming languages.

problem: Mixed-integer optimization solvers are slow on large problems; integrating machine learning models could accelerate them but method selection and hyperparameter tuning are challenging.
approach: PMVB uses a model-agnostic, multi-variable branching procedure that partitions the feasible region via data-driven hyperplanes, requiring minimal implementation overhead and compatible with any ML model.
contribution: PMVB integrates into state-of-the-art MIP solvers and demonstrates effectiveness in improving MIP-solving efficiency on classical benchmarks and real-world instances with interpretable hyperparameter strategies.

problem: Hypergraph contrastive learning emphasizes instance discrimination via hyperspherical uniformity, which pushes embeddings apart indiscriminately, causing semantic flattening where semantic depth of hyperedges collapses.
approach: HyperDepth coordinates spectral and geometric signals via decoupled spectral encoding with adaptive gating (high-frequency for instance discrimination, low-frequency for hierarchy) and an energy-based hierarchical alignment module with a learnable prototype tree.
contribution: Recovers semantic depth in hypergraph representations while retaining instance discrimination, with theoretical guarantees that spectral and hierarchical objectives operate on orthogonal components under a mild frequency-separation assumption.

problem: Auditory attention decoding from EEG in multi-speaker environments is hindered by overlooking phase information, which is crucial for distinguishing structured neural patterns from noise in the frequency domain.
approach: PCRNet introduces Temporal Context Calibration (TCC) to capture long-range temporal dependencies and Dual-Domain Integration (DDI) with phase-guided spectral filtering to dynamically refine real and imaginary components separately.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods on three public datasets, particularly under challenging ultra-short 0.1-second windows, via effective phase recalibration and enhanced feature discriminability.

problem: Diffusion large language models lack effective post-training techniques including reinforcement learning, and existing approaches rely on sequence-level optimization with biased likelihood approximations.
approach: AGRPO is a policy gradient algorithm that optimizes individual denoising steps rather than full sequences by leveraging the Markovian structure of dLLM generation, enabling unbiased gradient updates via a novel timestep estimation scheme.
contribution: Achieves absolute accuracy gains of +59.4% on Countdown and +69.7% on Sudoku over the base LLaDA model, exceeding comparable methods like diffu-GRPO on reasoning tasks.

problem: Rapid scientific idea production has not been matched by advances in idea evaluation; existing methods suffer from narrow knowledge horizons, flattened evaluation dimensions, and LLM-as-a-Judge bias.
approach: InnoEval treats idea evaluation as knowledge-grounded, multi-perspective reasoning via heterogeneous deep knowledge search (dynamic evidence from online sources), an innovation review board with reviewers of distinct backgrounds, and multi-dimensional decoupled evaluation.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on point-wise, pair-wise, and group-wise evaluation tasks with judgment patterns and consensus highly aligned with human experts.

problem: Understanding how cellular morphology, gene expression, and spatial context jointly shape tissue function requires analyzing high-resolution image-based spatial transcriptomics, but existing methods analyze modalities in isolation.
approach: SPATIA is a multi-level generative model that learns unified, spatially aware representations by fusing morphology, gene expression, and spatial context, incorporating confidence-aware optimal transport reweighting and morphology-profile alignment.
contribution: Benchmarked on 12 tasks spanning phenotype generation, annotation, clustering, gene imputation, and cross-modal prediction over 25.9M cell-gene pairs, improving generative fidelity by 8% and predictive accuracy up to 3%.

problem: Adapting foundation models to multimodal tasks in dual-stream architectures (unimodal encoders like DINO and BERT) remains challenging; parameter-efficient methods like LoRA operate within each modality in isolation, limiting cross-modal interactions.
approach: CoLA extends LoRA with a dedicated inter-modal adaptation pathway alongside the standard intra-modal pathway, enabling dual-path adaptation that captures cross-modal interactions without interference.
contribution: Achieves relative gains of ~3% on vision-language benchmarks (RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg) and ~2% on audio-visual (AVE, AVS) tasks while maintaining parameter efficiency, enabling the first multi-task PEFT framework for visual grounding.

problem: Large-scale learning systems must balance competing continuous objectives (fairness thresholds, diversity mixing rates) while minimizing system instability; existing frameworks only handle binary states.
approach: Lazy Graph-LinUCB extends continuous state optimization via dependency graphs capturing objective structure, with lazy updates to minimize switching costs, asynchronous scheduling, adaptive graph learning, and joint estimation leveraging data sharing.
contribution: Reduces movement costs by over a factor of three in heterogeneous systems while maintaining similar cumulative losses, enabling efficient multi-objective optimization with system stability.

problem: Continual test-time adaptation of LLMs to evolving domains requires balancing adaptability and stability; dense models and mixture-of-experts face routing difficulties for unseen domains and fail to capture domain-level shifts.
approach: TiME models MoE routing as test-time allocation via asymmetric co-optimal transport (As-COOT), with semantic space alignment via bidirectional contrastive learning and relaxed sample-side constraints to ensure noise robustness.
contribution: Outperforms baselines in continual test-time adaptation by correctly routing shifting domains and maintaining the adaptability-stability balance.

problem: Large language models provide wrong answers to negation-related questions despite internally possessing components for correct processing; understanding how they mechanistically process negation is unclear.
approach: The paper applies observational and causal interpretability techniques to reveal that models use both suppressive mechanisms (attending to negated phrases and suppressing concepts) and constructive mechanisms (building negative phrase representations as vectors), with construction being more prominent.
contribution: Shows that ablating late-layer attention modules greatly improves accuracy on negation questions, deepening understanding of LLM internals and highlighting construction-dominant computations and competing mechanisms.

problem: Large language models struggle with the strict procedural logic and accuracy required by biological protocols, limiting autonomous scientific experimentation capabilities.
approach: BioProBench provides a corpus of 27,000 human-written protocols and systematically constructed 550,000+ task instances for training and benchmarking; ProAgent grounds itself in BioProCorpus to improve reasoning, quantitative precision, and safety awareness.
contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of 10 mainstream LLMs reveals significant performance drops on tasks demanding deep reasoning and quantitative precision; ProAgent substantially advances state-of-the-art in procedural reasoning for biology.

problem: Neural network wavefunctions lack a systematic, reproducible benchmarking protocol and understanding of how representability depends on system size and model parameters.
approach: WF-Bench provides a benchmarking dataset spanning multiple strongly-correlated quantum matter regimes (topological states, Wigner crystals, superconducting wavefunctions) with a consistent protocol for target wavefunction matching and fidelity evaluation.
contribution: Discovers empirical scaling laws characterizing how representability depends on system size and key parameters (determinant count, model depth); unified framework guides design of future neural wavefunction architectures.

problem: Language models respond inconsistently to translation-equivalent prompts across languages, undermining reliability of multilingual systems; existing metrics lack information-theoretic foundations.
approach: The paper provides an information-theoretic definition of crosslingual consistency as a divergence bound and proposes Direct Consistency Optimization (DCO), a tractable off-policy surrogate to penalized consistency optimization that couples divergence with KL penalty to a reference model.
contribution: Across 26 languages and diverse LLMs, DCO significantly improves crosslingual consistency and outperforms existing methods, enabling targeted alignment of low-resource languages.

problem: Self-rewarding language models suffer from synchronized improvement of chosen and rejected responses that progressively narrows the representational difference between contrasting samples, undermining effective preference learning.
approach: Temporal Self-Rewarding LMs coordinate past, present, and future model generations: Anchored Rejection fixes rejected responses using the past model's outputs, and Future-Guided Chosen curates chosen samples using next-generation predictions.
contribution: Across Llama, Qwen, and Mistral model families, reaches 29.44 win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0 for Llama3.1-8B, outperforming self-rewarding baseline (19.69) by 9.75, with superior out-of-distribution generalization.

problem: Notification dispatch at scale requires balancing multiple outcomes, complex constraints (timing, presentation, budget, device quotas), and small-effect uplift estimation that is multidimensional.
approach: BUOPLR decouples uplift estimation from decision-making: first learns bundle-level, multi-outcome uplift via architecture capturing cross-treatment and cross-outcome relationships, then performs scalable assignment via decision-space restriction and Lagrangian relaxation.
contribution: Offline experiments outperform state-of-the-art methods; online A/B tests on Kuaishou (100M+ daily users) increase DAU by 0.5%.

problem: Large multimodal models have high inference-time overhead; existing pruning methods assume static visual evidence, but visual evidence is step-dependent during reasoning, and redundant context can steer models toward query-irrelevant regions.
approach: VisionPulse performs step-wise visual token pruning during reasoning by computing lightweight visual attention mass to estimate step-wise retention budget and retain only critical tokens, filtering redundant context.
contribution: Retains only 5% of visual tokens per step with reasoning traces shortened by 11.2% while keeping accuracy almost unchanged.

problem: Scene graph generation from visual data is limited by scarce annotations and long-tail distribution of relational predicates; training-free VLM-based methods produce hallucinated relations and flat graph structures.
approach: HSGG is training-free, combining bidirectional hierarchical entity perception (top-down expansion + bottom-up attributes) with geometry-guided relation reasoning: geometry-aware filtering prunes implausible pairs, geometry-grounded contrastive decoding suppresses hallucinations.
contribution: Generalizes effectively to unseen objects and predicates, substantially reduces relational hallucinations, and consistently improves downstream reasoning performance.

problem: Existing expressive power results for neural networks are derived under exact arithmetic and cannot apply to real floating-point implementations with finite precision and round-off errors.
approach: The paper studies floating-point ReLU networks with floating-point parameters and operations, investigating minimum depth and width to represent functions from floating-point vectors to floating-point numbers.
contribution: Shows minimum depth for representing all functions from Fd to F is exactly three; minimum width lies between 2d and 2d+4, with tighter bounds for non-negative floats (between d and d+4).

problem: Tail-end risk measures like conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) cannot admit recursive Bellman decomposition in MDPs because CVaR depends on entire trajectories, and standard state augmentation leads to sparse rewards and degenerate fixed points.
approach: Proposes novel state augmentation with a Bellman operator on L-infinity that produces dense per-step rewards and contracting properties on the full space of bounded value functions.
contribution: Develops risk-averse value iteration and Q-learning with convergence guarantees and discretization error bounds, enabling practical CVaR-sensitive policy learning with effective performance-safety trade-offs.

problem: Federated learning on heterogeneous devices with non-IID data faces parameter conflicts from stochastic sub-model selection and lacks diversity in rule-based neuron selection, preventing comprehensive parameter optimization.
approach: SpineFL decomposes each layer into mandatory backbone (shared by all sub-models) and dynamic portion, using activation-guided probabilistic neuron selection where neurons with higher historical activation are more likely selected.
contribution: Addresses parameter conflicts while maintaining model generalization through diverse neuron selection in heterogeneous federated learning settings.

problem: TabPFN, a foundation model for tabular datasets using in-context learning, is vulnerable to label shift and overfits to the majority class due to imbalanced training data.
approach: DistPFN performs test-time posterior adjustment by rescaling predicted class probabilities to downweight the training prior (context class distribution) and emphasize the model's predicted posterior; DistPFN-T adds temperature scaling for adaptive adjustment.
contribution: On 250+ OpenML datasets, demonstrates substantial improvements under label shift while maintaining strong performance in standard settings without label shift.

problem: Coverless image steganography lacks robust access control, making it difficult to selectively reveal hidden contents to different authorized users in multi-user settings.
approach: MIDAS is a training-free diffusion-based coverless steganography framework enabling multi-image hiding with user-specific access control via latent-level fusion, using Random Basis mechanism and Latent Vector Fusion module.
contribution: Consistently outperforms training-free baselines in access control functionality, stego image quality, robustness to noise, and resistance to steganalysis.

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs is computationally expensive; existing methods for controlling reasoning length either degrade quality or require complex training pipelines.
approach: Re-FORC trains a lightweight adapter to predict expected future rewards as a function of reasoning tokens, enabling early stopping, optimized model selection, and adaptive test-time scaling.
contribution: Enables early stopping reducing compute by up to 24%, optimized model/length selection that outperforms largest model alone by 1.7 points at 12% less compute, and 8.8 point accuracy gains via adaptive scaling.

problem: LLMs with chain-of-thought reasoning consume excessive tokens that inflate inference costs; existing efficiency methods degrade quality or require complex training.
approach: BCR trains the model to solve N problems simultaneously within a shared context, rewarded purely by per-instance accuracy, which creates an implicit token budget yielding task-scaling laws and enabling N as a controllable throughput dimension.
contribution: Identifies novel task-scaling law where per-problem token usage decreases monotonically with concurrent problems N; achieves 15.8-62.6% token reduction on math benchmarks while maintaining or improving accuracy (e.g., +13.3% on AIME25).

problem: The choice of action space in imitation-based robotic manipulation policy learning fundamentally shapes optimization landscape, yet remains guided by ad-hoc heuristics, leaving ambiguous understanding of design philosophies.
approach: Large-scale empirical study dissecting action design along temporal and spatial axes, examining absolute vs. delta representations and joint-space vs. task-space parameterizations via 13,000+ real-world rollouts and 500+ trained models.
contribution: Shows that delta action representation consistently improves performance, while joint-space and task-space offer complementary strengths favoring stability and generalization respectively.

problem: Aligning frozen pretrained vision and language models typically requires millions of paired samples with contrastive losses; semi-supervised settings with abundant unpaired data are underexplored.
approach: SOTAlign uses a two-stage framework: first, a linear teacher recovers coarse shared geometry from limited paired data, then refines alignment on unpaired samples via optimal-transport-based divergence that transfers relational structure.
contribution: Effectively leverages unpaired images and text to learn robust joint embeddings, significantly outperforming supervised and semi-supervised baselines across datasets and encoder pairs.

problem: Fine-tuning language models on narrowly scoped objectives can lead to emergent misalignment where the model learns the target behavior but also develops undesirable out-of-domain behaviors.
approach: BLOCK-EM identifies a small set of internal features that reliably control the misaligned behavior and constrains the model from strengthening these features during fine-tuning, blocking the mechanism driving misalignment.
contribution: Across six fine-tuning domains, achieves up to 95% relative reduction in emergent misalignment with no degradation in model quality or target-task performance.

problem: Inferring temporal processes from static single-cell RNA sequencing snapshots is challenging; current approaches using neural ODEs and flows are sensitive to overfitting and lack careful modeling of biological variability.
approach: Proposes generative framework modeling population trends via latent heteroscedastic Gaussian process (approximated by Hilbert space methods), with optimal transport objective aligning generated and observed distributions, incorporating cell-specific latent time and cell type conditioning.
contribution: Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on complex interpolation and extrapolation benchmarks with novel gradient-based strategy for inferring perturbation trajectories.

problem: Bisimulation-based visual RL uses fixed, pre-specified latent distance metrics (e.g., Lp norms) which may be overly restrictive, while unconstrained pairwise distances admit degenerate solutions.
approach: PAMD parameterizes a positive-definite, pair-conditioned metric for measuring latent state similarity that is more expressive than fixed metrics yet structured to avoid degeneracies, as a plug-in for bisimulation methods.
contribution: On visual MuJoCo continuous-control tasks, substantially improves final performance of several recent bisimulation-based RL algorithms when equipped with the adaptive distance metric.

problem: Omnimodal LLMs face prohibitive computational costs from processing continuous streaming inputs across video, audio, and text due to quadratic token complexity; existing compression strategies use biased modality-centric priors or uniform retention.
approach: OmniFit decouples interaction profiling from inference via Layer-Adaptive Heterogeneity Profiling (LAHP) to dynamically allocate budgets per layer based on redundancy, and Alignment-Rectified Token Selection (ARTS) to identify semantically aligned tokens.
contribution: Retains 98% of model performance with only 20% token usage, achieving up to 2.31x end-to-end speedup and 2.5x VRAM saving across 3 model series on 10 benchmarks.
